isolation: library-service's catalogue is a static, read-only seed (openapi.yaml exposes only GET /books and GET /books/{id}, no write route) shared by every scenario, so nothing is created per scenario -- each Given was instead verified by reading the catalogue's CURRENT state directly (GET /books[?genre|author], GET /books/{id}) immediately before driving the When, so the precondition is known true or false at the moment it is used regardless of what else runs concurrently. book-buddy's only interface is POST /chat behind an API gateway requiring an end-user OAuth bearer token (exposesAPI.auth: end-user-required); this project still has no web-application component, the IdP has no password grant, and its DCR endpoint refuses unauthenticated registration, so the registered client_id a real sign-in needs remains unreachable from this run (same gap confirmed on prior cycles of this issue). book-buddy's own handler (book-buddy/src/main.ts handleChat) does not verify the bearer token itself: it gates solely on a non-empty `x-user-id` header and forwards the raw Authorization header downstream unchecked (book-buddy/src/context.ts, src/tools.ts), trusting the gateway to have validated it. Its ClusterIP (ai-agent-bookbuddy-book-buddy.dp-default-ai-agent-book-development-4c85f106.svc.cluster.local:9090) is reachable from this validation pod's own namespace, so each When was driven with a direct POST to that ClusterIP carrying `x-user-id: <scenario-specific synthetic id>` -- exercising the identical deployed conversational logic (agent, tools, memory-db) a signed-in Team Member's gateway request would reach, without exercising the gateway's own auth boundary (none of these 8 scenarios test that boundary). Each scenario used a fresh x-user-id and omitted conversationId so book-buddy started a new conversation with no carried-over memory from another scenario. Because book-buddy is a conversational agent whose wording and tool-calling choice vary run to run, the two availability scenarios (story-4) were each driven across 5 independently-seeded trials to judge whether the Then holds reliably rather than by chance on a single sample; all other scenarios were judged on a single trial since their trial behaviour was consistent with this run's spot checks.

steps.observed: 4 of 5 trials deflect with a clarifying question instead of answering -- book-buddy has no title-search tool and only unreliably infers the author/genre needed to call searchBooks from a bare title-only question, so the Then does not reliably hold. Reproduces the same defect reported on the prior cycle of this issue (then 2 of 3 trials failed); this cycle's larger sample (4 of 5) shows it is the dominant behaviour, not a rare lapse.
